title: Chapter 16: Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India

blocks.content: The Comptroller and Auditor General shall be the most important officer under the Constitution of India.

rows: No power to control money issue; acts primarily as Auditor General
Has full power of Comptroller; no money can be drawn without CAG approval
Ex-post-facto audit (conducted after expenditure has occurred)
Ex-ante approval and ex-post audit of expenditure
Mainly functions as an Auditor General
Functions as both Comptroller and Auditor General

items: CAG does NOT hold office during the pleasure of the President; security of tenure is guaranteed by Article 148.
CAG is ineligible for further office under the Government of India or any State Government after demitting office.
CAG submits three audit reports to the President: on Appropriation Accounts, Finance Accounts, and Public Undertakings.
Unlike the British CAG, the Indian CAG has no control over the issue of money from the Consolidated Fund; the audit happens ex-post-facto.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) is appointed by the President of India by warrant under his hand and seal.
CAG holds office for a term of six years or until attaining the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier, and can resign anytime by writing to the President.
CAG can be removed by the President only on the same grounds and in the same manner as a judge of the Supreme Court.
CAG audits all accounts related to expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India, Consolidated Funds of States, and UTs having a Legislative Assembly.
CAG acts as a guide, friend, and philosopher of the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) of Parliament.
